gaps.title: Agent-facing descriptions claim calibrated probabilities the shipped checkpoints do not have
gaps.case: laya/mcp/server.py:95-101 tells every MCP client 'noul (calibrated P(true))' and 'No text generation, so no hallucination'; pyproject.toml:8 says 'with calibrated probabilities'. README.md:1578-1580 and research/results/t4_colab_benchmark.json (calibration_repair.mean_ece_shipped 0.4656 for laya, 0.3135 for laya-multilingual, which ships all-1.0 temperatures) show both checkpoints over-confident as shipped.
gaps.impact: Agents and integrators that read tool descriptions, not the README, act on raw probabilities as if calibrated (OWASP LLM09 misinformation); confident wrong answers are framed as impossible.
gaps.fix: Reword the descriptions and package metadata to 'probabilities; fit temperatures before thresholding', ship fitted temperatures for laya-multilingual, and add a test that fails when a description claims calibration that the checkpoint's evidence state (laya/evidence.py) does not show.

gaps.title: Checkpoints, datasets and the regression baseline are unpinned by default
gaps.case: laya/revisions.py:77-79 returns no revision unless the caller or LAYA_REVISION asks; docs/security.md:3-6 confirms the Hub default revision is used. The weekly gate runs research/eval/laya_eval.py --model convaiinnovations/laya with no revision (.github/workflows/evals.yml:54-58), datasets load without a revision (research/eval/laya_eval.py:104), and the baseline research/results/eval_english_51_languages.json records no model revision.
gaps.impact: A changed or compromised Hub repository changes every default deployment's decisions (including guardrail presets), and the regression gate silently compares against a moving target.
gaps.fix: Default the published checkpoints to PINNED_REVISIONS with an explicit opt-out, pin dataset revisions in the harnesses, and write model and dataset revisions into every report and baseline.

gaps.title: laya-serve listens on all interfaces without authentication by default
gaps.case: laya/serve.py:23 and laya/serve.py:1593 default LAYA_HOST to 0.0.0.0; laya/serve.py:39 leaves LAYA_API_KEY unset, which disables authentication; SECURITY.md:64-66 documents this as a warning rather than changing it.
gaps.impact: Unauthenticated network access to inference and server metadata on any host where laya-serve is started without extra configuration; conflicts with the CRA secure-by-default obligation from Dec 2027.
gaps.fix: Default to 127.0.0.1, and refuse to bind a non-loopback address without LAYA_API_KEY unless an explicit opt-out flag is set; test both in tests/test_serve.py.

gaps.title: Headline accuracy and throughput claims without committed results
gaps.case: README.md:89 presents 0.766 (fine-tuned) against 0.362 with no caveat; tests/test_doc_tables.py:362-367 lists 'README.md typed-decisions rows: no committed artifact for the fine-tuned checkpoint' and 'README.md / BENCHMARKS.md 103-332 q/s throughput: hand-picked from a range spanning 55-553'.
gaps.impact: The most prominent accuracy claim and the throughput claim cannot be reproduced from the repository.
gaps.fix: Commit the fine-tuning evaluation output (seed, n, checkpoint revision) and generate the README cells from it; replace the throughput range with the measured distribution from a committed file.

gaps.title: Calibration comparison with Jev is not on matched data
gaps.case: README.md:1505 claims ECE 0.081 vs 0.246, '3x better'. 0.081 is the mean over 49 suites after a per-suite refit (t4_colab_benchmark.json calibration_repair.laya.mean_ece_refit 0.0812); 0.246 comes from a different third-party study (research/README.md:176-177). On the one shared benchmark Jev's published ECE 0.144 is lower than laya-typed-decisions' 0.213 (README.md:1526-1531).

gaps.title: Supported-versions table is stale and no regulatory position exists

gaps.title: Batch scoring and training cannot resume after a crash
gaps.case: laya/cli.py:361-404 builds every request, makes one predict_batch call (line 398) and prints only after it returns; laya/train.py:1125-1130 saves checkpoint_latest per epoch but 'rg -n -i resume laya/' finds no resume path.

opportunities.title: Publish the typed-decision record as a versioned JSON Schema
opportunities.description: The answer object (choice/score/noul, probabilities, answer_confidence, abstention state and threshold, usage with truncation and collapsed options, routing) is consistent across the Python host, its ports and laya-coreml, but exists only in code and prose. A published schema lets REA/rex evidence records, strix-style coverage ledgers and agent harnesses (orca, t3code, pandacode, pi) consume decisions without reading prose, and lets contract drift fail CI.

opportunities.title: Extract a torch-free calibration and abstention kernel
opportunities.description: Temperature fitting, binning, per-bucket abstention thresholds at a target error and the confidence gate are numpy logic, but laya/calibrate.py imports torch at module scope, so laya's own evidence module cannot import it and laya-coreml carries a modified copy with lazy imports. my-jev's bench.py and RE4exa rex's epistemics.calibrate (Wilson intervals, target-error advice) reimplement the same metrics. One small package would serve all four and add the per-class intervals laya lacks.

opportunities.title: Cut the MCP catalog and make its claims honest
opportunities.description: Move the repeated guardrail, model and controls text into one resource, add readOnly annotations and replace 'calibrated P(true)' and 'no hallucination' with measured wording. The same server is copied byte-for-byte into laya-coreml, so the fix reaches both.
evidence: AST measurement: >=12,613 description bytes, ~10 KB repeated

opportunities.title: One array-based backend contract for every host
opportunities.description: The backend contract hands torch tensors to a backend, so the ONNX path is a second host class and the Core ML and MLX ports copy the whole host (router, serve, MCP, evals, hooks) and re-sync it by hand. An array-in/array-out contract would let ONNX, Core ML, MLX and future runtimes plug in without duplicating host semantics.

opportunities.title: Guard-plus-abstention screen for agent harnesses, measured on their own fixtures
opportunities.description: agent-sandbox-lockdown already has human approval for writes, a JSONL tool-call log and a planted document-shaped prompt injection. laya's guard preset with abstention could screen tool outputs before they reach the LLM and route low-confidence cases to the existing approval step. #781 shows the guard misses document-shaped injections, so the composition should start as a held-out benchmark on that fixture, not as a safety claim.

opportunities.title: Offline, on-device typed decisions with declared cost per decision
opportunities.description: laya already runs offline (HF_HUB_OFFLINE, ModelScope mirror), in the browser through ONNX Runtime Web, and on Apple Silicon through laya-coreml, which measures joules per decision. Publishing latency and energy per checkpoint and runtime would let the Router pick the cheapest adequate path as on-device inference and energy pricing become requirements.

questions: Are laya's accuracy and calibration claims backed by reproducible evaluations? Mostly: harnesses, seeds, n and dates are committed and a CI test checks table cells against result files, and the 0.466 -> 0.081 ECE refit is out of sample. Exceptions: the fine-tuned 0.766 headline and the 103-332 q/s range have no committed result, and the 'ECE 3x better than Jev' row compares different studies.

Do shipped probabilities support abstention without refitting? No. Both checkpoints ship over-confident and laya-multilingual has no fitted temperatures; abstention is opt-in. The tooling to fit temperatures and target-error thresholds is present and tested.

Are code, weights and data licences clear? Code is Apache-2.0 with SPDX identifiers. The weights' Apache-2.0 licence is asserted only in a README table, and the base-encoder and training-data licences (training mix includes AG News and BoolQ) are not documented in the repository; Hugging Face model cards were not reachable.

Runtime behaviour of laya-serve and the MCP server (not run); the MCP catalog size is a static lower bound (3 of 10 descriptions not resolvable without import).

scope_notes: Profile ml-system: three checkpoints plus their inference runtimes, ports and evaluation harness. uses_llm=true because laya ships an MCP server and agent-framework integrations executed by agents (it calls no LLM); executes_code=false because the shipped package is CI-gated against subprocess/eval and only dev scripts spawn processes; has_ui=false because the web playground is an example outside the published package; network_service (laya-serve), parses_untrusted (HTTP bodies, Hub model files), heavy_compute (GPU training and inference) and distributed (PyPI, npm, Maven) are true; uses_crypto=false because cryptography is limited to SHA-256 integrity digests and constant-time token comparison, with no signing, encryption or key exchange for SEC-9 to assess. Static review at ffc1420 (shallow clone); weights on Hugging Face were not reachable, so behaviour claims were checked against committed result files, not reruns.
